### Problem `#140` (`Int-2`): Luogu P4307 [JSOI2009] — 球队收益 / 球队预算 (Team Revenue)

- **Judge / URL:** [Luogu P4307](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P4307) (`[JSOI2009] 球队收益 / 球队预算`)
- **Constraints:** $N \le 5000$ teams, $M \le 1000$ remaining matches. Each team $i$ has initial wins $w_i^{(0)}$, initial losses $l_i^{(0)}$, and non-negative cost coefficients $C_i, D_i$. Time limit $1.0\text{ s}$.
- **Task:** Decide the winner of each of the $M$ remaining matches to minimize total league expenditure $\sum_{i=1}^N (C_i w_i^2 + D_i l_i^2)$.

#### 4-Step Compilation

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal):** Two-variable quadratic cost $C_i w_i^2 + D_i l_i^2$ per team with fixed total games $w_i + l_i = G_i$. Directly matches Section 2 (**Win–Loss Substitution**).
2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Model):** Pre-assume all $\text{rem}_i$ remaining games for team $i$ are losses: $L_i = l_i^{(0)} + \text{rem}_i$ and $\text{BaseCost} = \sum_{i=1}^N \bigl(C_i (w_i^{(0)})^2 + D_i L_i^2\bigr)$. Winning the $k$-th game ($k = 1, \dots, \text{rem}_i$) transitions $(w, l) = (w_i^{(0)} + k - 1,\; L_i - k + 1) \to (w+1, l-1)$ with marginal cost

   $$
   \Delta \Phi_i(k) \;=\; C_i(2w + 1) - D_i(2l - 1).
   $$

3. **Step 3 (Graph Construction & Potential Initialization):**
   - For each match $m = \{u, v\}$ ($1 \le m \le M$): add $S \to \text{Match}_m$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=0$) and arcs $\text{Match}_m \to \text{Team}_u, \text{Match}_m \to \text{Team}_v$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=0$).
   - For each team $i$ and $k \in \{1, \dots, \text{rem}_i\}$: add arc $\text{Team}_i \to T$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=\Delta \Phi_i(k)$).
   - Because $\Delta \Phi_i(k)$ can be negative when $D_i(2l - 1) > C_i(2w + 1)$, set the initial 3-layer DAG potential $\pi(T) = \min\bigl(0LL,\; \min_{i : \text{rem}_i > 0} \Delta \Phi_i(1)\bigr)$ and $\pi(v) = 0$ for all $v \neq T$.
4. **Step 4 (Complexity):** Only $M \le 1000$ units of flow are routed, and only $2M \le 2000$ marginal arcs $\text{Team}_i \to T$ are ever created across all teams! Thus Primal-Dual Dijkstra runs $1000$ times on a graph with $\le 6002$ vertices and $\le 5000$ arcs, finishing in $< 20\text{ ms}$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 1 (#140) — Decoupling Wins and Losses"}
Notice that $w_i + l_i$ is already determined before any remaining match is played! What is $l_i$ if team $i$ loses *all* $\text{rem}_i$ of its remaining matches?
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 2 (#140) — Marginal Cost of Converting One Loss into One Win"}
Suppose team $i$ currently has $w$ wins and $l$ losses. If we change the outcome of one of team $i$'s matches from a loss to a win, $(w, l)$ becomes $(w+1, l-1)$. Expand $C_i(w+1)^2 + D_i(l-1)^2 - (C_i w^2 + D_i l^2)$ and check that this increment increases by $2(C_i + D_i) \ge 0$ for each subsequent win.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 3 (#140) — Fast Dijkstra Initialization with Negative Marginals"}
Because all negative-cost arcs enter the sink $T$ directly from $\text{Team}_i$, the initial network is a DAG of depth $3$. Setting $\pi(T) = \min(0, \min_i \Delta \Phi_i(1))$ and $\pi = 0$ everywhere else makes every initial reduced cost non-negative in $O(N)$ time without SPFA!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#140 — Luogu P4307 [JSOI2009] 球队收益)"}
```cpp
void solve_jsoi2009_team_revenue() {
    int n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return;

    vector<long long> w0(n), l0(n), C(n), D(n);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) cin >> w0[i] >> l0[i] >> C[i] >> D[i];

    vector<pair<int, int>> matches(m);
    vector<int> rem(n, 0);
    for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
        int u, v;
        cin >> u >> v;
        --u; --v;
        matches[j] = {u, v};
        rem[u]++;
        rem[v]++;
    }

    int S = 0, T = n + m + 1;
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    for (int j = 0; j < m; ++j) {
        int m_node = n + 1 + j;
        mcmf.add_edge(S, m_node, 1, 0);
        mcmf.add_edge(m_node, matches[j].first + 1, 1, 0);
        mcmf.add_edge(m_node, matches[j].second + 1, 1, 0);
    }

    long long base_cost = 0, min_delta = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        long long L = l0[i] + rem[i];
        base_cost += C[i] * w0[i] * w0[i] + D[i] * L * L;
        for (int k = 1; k <= rem[i]; ++k) {
            long long w = w0[i] + k - 1;
            long long l = L - k + 1;
            long long delta = C[i] * (2 * w + 1) - D[i] * (2 * l - 1);
            mcmf.add_edge(i + 1, T, 1, delta);
            min_delta = min(min_delta, delta);
        }
    }

    // 3-layer DAG potential initialization: makes all initial reduced costs >= 0
    mcmf.pi[T] = min_delta;
    cout << base_cost + mcmf.solve(S, T).second << "\n";
}
```

### Problem `#141` (`Adv-1`): Codeforces 863 F — Almost Permutation

- **Judge / URL:** [Codeforces 863F](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/863/F)
- **Constraints:** $N \le 50$, $Q \le 100$ constraints. Array elements $a_1, \dots, a_N \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ initially satisfy $1 \le a_i \le N$. Each query is either `1 l r v` ($\forall i \in [l, r],\; a_i \ge v$) or `2 l r v` ($\forall i \in [l, r],\; a_i \le v$). Time limit $1.0\text{ s}$.
- **Task:** Assign each $a_i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ satisfying all $Q$ constraints to minimize the sum of squared frequencies $\sum_{v=1}^N \text{cnt}(v)^2$, where $\text{cnt}(v) = \sum_{i=1}^N [a_i = v]$, or print `-1` if no valid array exists.

#### 4-Step Compilation

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal):** Each position $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ must choose one value $v$ from its allowed interval $[L_i, R_i]$, and the objective $\sum_{v=1}^N \text{cnt}(v)^2$ is the sum of squares of the in-degrees of the value vertices $v$.
2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Model):** Intersect all $Q$ bounds for each position $i$:

   $$
   L_i = \max\bigl(1,\; \max_{(1, l, r, v) : l \le i \le r} v\bigr), \qquad R_i = \min\bigl(N,\; \min_{(2, l, r, v) : l \le i \le r} v\bigr).
   $$

   If $L_i > R_i$ for any $i$, output `-1` immediately. Otherwise, since $\text{cnt}(v)^2 = \sum_{k=1}^{\text{cnt}(v)} (2k - 1)$, the $k$-th occurrence of value $v$ incurs marginal cost $2k - 1$.
3. **Step 3 (Graph Construction):**
   - Source $S \to \text{Pos}_i$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=0$) for $i = 1, \dots, N$.
   - $\text{Pos}_i \to \text{Val}_v$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=0$) for each $v \in [L_i, R_i]$.
   - $\text{Val}_v \to T$: $N$ parallel unit-capacity arcs with costs $1, 3, 5, \dots, 2N - 1$ for $k = 1, \dots, N$.
4. **Step 4 (Verification):** All costs are positive odd integers $2k - 1 \ge 1$. Route $N$ units from $S$ to $T$; if maximum flow $< N$ (which only happens if $L_i > R_i$), output `-1`, else output $\text{MinCost}$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 1 (#141) — Simplifying the $Q$ Range Constraints"}
Since each constraint applies a lower or upper bound to individual elements $a_i$ independently, you can maintain `L[i]` and `R[i]` for each index $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ by taking `L[i] = max(L[i], v)` on type-1 queries and `R[i] = min(R[i], v)` on type-2 queries.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 2 (#141) — Expanding $\text{cnt}(v)^2$ into Odd Marginal Costs"}
Use the identity $c^2 = 1 + 3 + 5 + \dots + (2c - 1)$. How much does the $k$-th element assigned to value $v$ increase $\text{cnt}(v)^2$?
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 3 (#141) — Bipartite Assignment + Convex Sink Bundle"}
Build a bipartite graph with $N$ position nodes on the left and $N$ value nodes on the right. Connect each value node $v$ to the sink $T$ with $N$ parallel edges of capacity $1$ and costs $1, 3, 5, \dots, 2N - 1$.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#141 — Codeforces 863F Almost Permutation)"}
```cpp
// Uses ConvexMCMF from Section 5.1
void solve_cf863f() {
    int n, q;
    if (!(cin >> n >> q)) return;

    vector<int> L(n + 1, 1), R(n + 1, n);
    for (int k = 0; k < q; ++k) {
        int type, l, r, v;
        cin >> type >> l >> r >> v;
        for (int i = l; i <= r; ++i) {
            if (type == 1) L[i] = max(L[i], v);
            else R[i] = min(R[i], v);
        }
    }

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        if (L[i] > R[i]) {
            cout << -1 << "\n";
            return;
        }
    }

    int S = 0, T = 2 * n + 1;
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        mcmf.add_edge(S, i, 1, 0);
        for (int v = L[i]; v <= R[i]; ++v) mcmf.add_edge(i, n + v, 1, 0);
    }
    for (int v = 1; v <= n; ++v) {
        mcmf.add_quadratic_bundle(n + v, T, n, 1, 0); // cnt(v)^2 = sum (2k - 1)
    }

    auto [flow, cost] = mcmf.solve(S, T);
    cout << (flow == n ? cost : -1) << "\n";
}
```

### Problem `#142` (`Adv-2`): Luogu P2517 [HAOI2010] — 订购 (Order) & Luogu P2488 [SDOI2011] — 工作安排 (Work Arrangement)

- **Judge / URL:** [Luogu P2517](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P2517) (`[HAOI2010] 订购`) & [Luogu P2488](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P2488) (`[SDOI2011] 工作安排`)
- **Constraints:**
  - **Part A (`[HAOI2010] 订购`):** $N \le 50$ months; month $i$ has customer demand $U_i \le 10^4$, unit purchasing cost $d_i$, warehouse storage fee $m$ per unit carried over from month $i$ to month $i+1$, and warehouse capacity $S_{\text{cap}} \le 10^4$. Minimize total purchasing and storage cost.
  - **Part B (`[SDOI2011] 工作安排`):** $M \le 250$ employees and $N \le 250$ product types (demands $C_j$). Each employee $i$ has $K_i + 1 \le 6$ piecewise-linear anger/wage brackets defined by thresholds $0 = T_{i,0} < T_{i,1} < \dots < T_{i,K_i} < T_{i,K_i+1} = \infty$ and strictly increasing per-unit anger slopes $W_{i,1} < W_{i,2} < \dots < W_{i,K_i+1}$. Minimize total anger across all employees.

#### 4-Step Compilation

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal):**
   - In `[HAOI2010] 订购`, each month $i$ is a time-indexed conservation node: goods ordered in month $i$ at cost $d_i$ can either satisfy month $i$'s demand $U_i$ immediately or be carried over to month $i+1$ along a capacity-$S_{\text{cap}}$ inventory edge of cost $m$.
   - In `[SDOI2011] 工作安排`, an employee's anger is a piecewise-linear convex function of their total workload $f_i = \sum_j f_{i,j}$, with up to $6$ constant-slope brackets $[T_{i,k-1}, T_{i,k}]$.
2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Model & Interval Bundling):**
   - For `[HAOI2010] 订购`: let $x_i \ge 0$ be the amount ordered in month $i$ and $I_i \in [0, S_{\text{cap}}]$ be the inventory carried from month $i$ to month $i+1$. Flow conservation at month $i$ is $x_i + I_{i-1} = U_i + I_i$, minimizing $\sum_{i=1}^N d_i x_i + \sum_{i=1}^{N-1} m I_i$.
   - For `[SDOI2011] 工作安排`: instead of creating $\sum C_j \le 2.5 \times 10^5$ unit-capacity arcs per employee, apply **Pattern 3 (Interval Bundling)** from Section 1.2! Bundle the $k$-th bracket of employee $i$ into a single arc $S \to \text{Emp}_i$ of capacity $T_{i,k} - T_{i,k-1}$ and cost $W_{i,k}$ (with capacity $\infty$ on the last bracket $k = K_i + 1$).
3. **Step 3 (Graph Construction):**
   - `[HAOI2010] 订购`: For $i = 1, \dots, N$, add ordering arc $S \to \text{Month}_i$ ($\text{cap}=\infty, \text{cost}=d_i$), demand arc $\text{Month}_i \to T$ ($\text{cap}=U_i, \text{cost}=0$), and (for $i < N$) carryover arc $\text{Month}_i \to \text{Month}_{i+1}$ ($\text{cap}=S_{\text{cap}}, \text{cost}=m$).
   - `[SDOI2011] 工作安排`: Add $K_i + 1$ bundled bracket arcs $S \to \text{Emp}_i$ ($\text{cap}=T_{i,k} - T_{i,k-1}, \text{cost}=W_{i,k}$), capability arcs $\text{Emp}_i \to \text{Prod}_j$ ($\text{cap}=\infty, \text{cost}=0$ if employee $i$ can make product $j$), and demand arcs $\text{Prod}_j \to T$ ($\text{cap}=C_j, \text{cost}=0$).
4. **Step 4 (Verification):** Both graphs have strictly non-negative initial edge costs ($d_i, m \ge 0$ and $W_{i,1} < \dots < W_{i,K_i+1}$ with $W_{i,1} \ge 0$), so Primal-Dual Dijkstra runs with $\pi \equiv 0$ in $< 15\text{ ms}$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 1 (#142) — Time-Expanded Inventory Carryover (`[HAOI2010] 订购`)"}
Model each month $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ as a vertex. Purchasing in month $i$ is an edge $S \to i$ of capacity $\infty$ and cost $d_i$; satisfying demand in month $i$ is an edge $i \to T$ of capacity $U_i$ and cost $0$. How do you represent storing up to $S_{\text{cap}}$ units from month $i$ to month $i+1$ at unit cost $m$?
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 2 (#142) — Bundling Piecewise-Linear Wage Brackets (`[SDOI2011] 工作安排`)"}
If an employee's marginal anger is $W_{i,1}$ for the first $T_{i,1}$ items, $W_{i,2}$ for the next $T_{i,2} - T_{i,1}$ items, and so on with $W_{i,1} < W_{i,2} < \dots$, you do *not* need unit-capacity edges! Just add $K_i + 1$ parallel edges from $S$ to $\text{Emp}_i$, where the $k$-th edge has capacity $T_{i,k} - T_{i,k-1}$ and cost $W_{i,k}$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 3 (#142) — Watch Out for 64-Bit Overflow"}
In `[SDOI2011] 工作安排`, total product demand $\sum C_j$ can reach $2.5 \times 10^5$ and anger slopes $W_{i,k}$ can reach $10^5$, so total minimum anger can exceed $2^{31} - 1$. Accumulate total cost in `long long`.
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#142A — Luogu P2517 [HAOI2010] 订购)"}
```cpp
// Uses ConvexMCMF from Section 5.1
void solve_haoi2010_order() {
    const long long INF = 1e15;
    int n;
    long long m_fee, S_cap;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m_fee >> S_cap)) return;

    vector<long long> U(n + 1), d(n + 1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> U[i];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) cin >> d[i];

    int S = 0, T = n + 1;
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        mcmf.add_edge(S, i, INF, d[i]);
        mcmf.add_edge(i, T, U[i], 0);
        if (i < n) mcmf.add_edge(i, i + 1, S_cap, m_fee);
    }

    cout << mcmf.solve(S, T).second << "\n";
}
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#142B — Luogu P2488 [SDOI2011] 工作安排)"}
```cpp
// Uses ConvexMCMF from Section 5.1
void solve_sdoi2011_work() {
    const long long INF = 1e15;
    int M, N;
    if (!(cin >> M >> N)) return;

    int S = 0, T = M + N + 1;
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    for (int j = 1; j <= N; ++j) {
        long long C_j;
        cin >> C_j;
        mcmf.add_edge(M + j, T, C_j, 0);
    }

    for (int i = 1; i <= M; ++i) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= N; ++j) {
            int can_make;
            cin >> can_make;
            if (can_make) mcmf.add_edge(i, M + j, INF, 0);
        }
    }

    for (int i = 1; i <= M; ++i) {
        int K;
        cin >> K;
        vector<long long> thresh(K + 2, 0), slope(K + 1, 0);
        for (int k = 1; k <= K; ++k) cin >> thresh[k];
        thresh[K + 1] = INF;
        for (int k = 0; k <= K; ++k) cin >> slope[k];

        // Pattern 3: Bundle each constant-slope interval [thresh[k], thresh[k+1]] into 1 arc
        mcmf.add_bracket_bundle(S, i, thresh, slope);
    }

    cout << mcmf.solve(S, T).second << "\n";
}
```

### Problem `#143` (`Mas-1`): Piecewise-Linear Large-Capacity Convex Cost Flow ($2^k$ Bit-Scaling) & AtCoder AGC 034 D — Manhattan Max Matching

- **Judge / URL:** [AtCoder AGC 034D](https://atcoder.jp/contests/agc034/tasks/agc034_d) (*Manhattan Max Matching*) & Large-Capacity Piecewise-Linear Convex MCMF (`Algorithm 18.1`)
- **Constraints:**
  - **Part A (Large-Capacity Piecewise-Linear Convex Cost Flow via $2^k$ Bit-Scaling):** Directed network with $V \le 400$, $E \le 1500$ piecewise-linear convex edges with capacities $U_e \le 10^9$ and costs $\le 10^9$.
  - **Part B (`AtCoder AGC 034D — Manhattan Max Matching`):** $N \le 1000$ red points $(R X_i, R Y_i)$ with multiplicity $R C_i \le 10$ and $N \le 1000$ blue points $(B X_j, B Y_j)$ with multiplicity $B C_j \le 10$ ($\sum R C_i = \sum B C_j \le 10^4$). Pair all red and blue tokens to **maximize** the sum of Manhattan distances $|R X_i - B X_j| + |R Y_i - B Y_j|$.

#### 4-Step Compilation

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal):**
   - In Part A, $U_e \le 10^9$ makes standard unit-step SSP `TLE`, requiring **Algorithm 18.1 (Edmonds–Karp Binary Capacity Bit-Scaling)**.
   - In Part B (`AGC 034D`), building all $N^2 = 10^6$ red-to-blue bipartite edges gives a dense graph that is too slow for $10^4$ flow units. However, the $\ell_1$ Manhattan distance $|x_1 - x_2| + |y_1 - y_2|$ is the maximum of four linear sign combinations:

     $$
     |x_1 - x_2| + |y_1 - y_2| \;=\; \max_{s_x, s_y \in \{-1, +1\}} \Bigl[\bigl(s_x x_1 + s_y y_1\bigr) + \bigl(-s_x x_2 - s_y y_2\bigr)\Bigr].
     $$

2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Model & 4-Sign Hub Factorization):**
   Introduce **4 intermediate sign-hub vertices** $H_0, H_1, H_2, H_3$ corresponding to $(s_x, s_y) \in \{(+1, +1), (+1, -1), (-1, +1), (-1, -1)\}$. Every red point $i$ connects to each hub $H_b$ with cost $-(s_x R X_i + s_y R Y_i)$, and each hub $H_b$ connects to every blue point $j$ with cost $-(-s_x B X_j - s_y B Y_j)$! Because we minimize negated cost (which maximizes the sum), the shortest path from Red $i$ to Blue $j$ through $\{H_0, H_1, H_2, H_3\}$ automatically picks the sign pair $(s_x, s_y)$ achieving the maximum $= |R X_i - B X_j| + |R Y_i - B Y_j|$!
3. **Step 3 (Graph Construction):**
   - For Part A (`Algorithm 18.1`): bundle each piecewise-linear convex edge into linear bracket arcs, add feedback arc $T \to S$ of capacity $\sum u_a$ and cost $-M_\infty$, and run bit-scaling from $k = \lfloor \log_2 U_{\max} \rfloor$ down to $0$.
   - For Part B (`AGC 034D`): $2N + 6$ vertices ($S$, $T$, $N$ Red, $N$ Blue, $4$ Hubs) and only $10N \approx 10^4$ edges! Initialize DAG potentials in $O(N)$ time along the 4-layer DAG $S \to \text{Red}_i \to H_b \to \text{Blue}_j \to T$ and run Primal-Dual Dijkstra.
4. **Step 4 (Verification):** In `AGC 034D`, since a path could theoretically bounce $\text{Red}_1 \to H_b \to \text{Red}_2$ in the residual graph after augmentations, the 4-hub graph has $O(N)$ vertices and $O(N)$ edges, so $O(F \cdot N \log N)$ with $F \le 10^4, N \le 1000$ takes $\approx 40\text{ ms}$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 1 (#143) — Binary Bit-Scaling Invariant (`Algorithm 18.1`)"}
When you double all arc capacities and flows ($f_a \gets 2 f_a, u_a \gets 2 u_a$), no new residual arcs appear, so $c_{uv}^\pi \ge 0$ continues to hold everywhere. A violation can only occur when you add $+1$ to the capacity of a currently saturated arc $(u \to v)$ whose reduced cost $c_{uv}^\pi$ is negative!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 2 (#143) — Repairing a Single-Bit Violation via Dijkstra"}
When unlocking $+1$ capacity on $(u \to v)$ exposes $c_{uv}^\pi < 0$, run Dijkstra from $v$ to $u$ in the *existing* residual graph (before adding the new capacity unit), update $\pi(x) \gets \pi(x) + \text{dist}(x)$, and if $\text{dist}(u) + c_{uv} + \pi_{\text{old}}(u) - \pi_{\text{old}}(v) < 0$, push $1$ unit along $u \to v \leadsto u$.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 3 (#143) — Expanding $|x_1 - x_2| + |y_1 - y_2|$ via 4 Hub Nodes (`AGC 034D`)"}
Use $|A| + |B| = \max(A+B, A-B, -A+B, -A-B)$. Create 4 hub vertices in the middle of the bipartite graph; connect every Red node to all 4 hubs and all 4 hubs to every Blue node, slashing the edge count from $N^2 = 10^6$ to $8N = 8000$!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#143A — 2^k Capacity Bit-Scaling for Large-Capacity Convex MCMF)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const long long INF = 4e18;

// Edmonds-Karp 2^k Binary Capacity Bit-Scaling (Algorithm 18.1)
// Handles arbitrary capacities U <= 10^9 and negative costs/cycles in O(E log U (E + V log V))
struct BitScalingMCMF {
    struct InternalEdge {
        int to, rev;
        long long cap, cost;
    };
    struct InputArc {
        int u, v, idx;
        long long full_cap, cost;
    };

    int n;
    vector<vector<InternalEdge>> adj;
    vector<InputArc> arcs;
    vector<long long> pi, dist;
    vector<int> pv_v, pv_e;

    BitScalingMCMF(int n) : n(n), adj(n), pi(n, 0), dist(n), pv_v(n), pv_e(n) {}

    int add_arc(int u, int v, long long cap, long long cost) {
        int idx = (int)adj[u].size();
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), 0, cost});
        adj[v].push_back({u, idx, 0, -cost});
        arcs.push_back({u, v, idx, cap, cost});
        return (int)arcs.size() - 1;
    }

    void dijkstra(int src) {
        fill(dist.begin(), dist.end(), INF);
        priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>> pq;
        dist[src] = 0;
        pq.push({0, src});
        while (!pq.empty()) {
            auto [d, u] = pq.top();
            pq.pop();
            if (d != dist[u]) continue;
            for (int i = 0; i < (int)adj[u].size(); ++i) {
                const auto& e = adj[u][i];
                if (e.cap > 0) {
                    long long nd = d + e.cost + pi[u] - pi[e.to];
                    if (nd < dist[e.to]) {
                        dist[e.to] = nd;
                        pv_v[e.to] = u;
                        pv_e[e.to] = i;
                        pq.push({nd, e.to});
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        long long max_d = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) if (dist[i] < INF) max_d = max(max_d, dist[i]);
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            pi[i] += (dist[i] < INF ? dist[i] : max_d);
        }
    }

    // Adds +1 unit of capacity to adj[u][idx] while maintaining c^pi >= 0
    void unlock_one_unit(int u, int idx) {
        auto& e = adj[u][idx];
        int v = e.to;
        if (e.cap > 0 || e.cost + pi[u] - pi[v] >= 0) {
            e.cap += 1;
            return;
        }
        dijkstra(v);
        if (dist[u] < INF && e.cost + pi[u] - pi[v] < 0) {
            // Augment 1 unit around the negative cycle u -> v ~> u
            adj[v][e.rev].cap += 1;
            for (int cur = u; cur != v; cur = pv_v[cur]) {
                int p = pv_v[cur], ei = pv_e[cur];
                adj[p][ei].cap -= 1;
                adj[cur][adj[p][ei].rev].cap += 1;
            }
        } else {
            e.cap += 1;
        }
    }

    pair<long long, long long> solve_st(int s, int t) {
        long long max_cap = 0, sum_cap = 0, max_cost = 1;
        for (const auto& a : arcs) {
            max_cap = max(max_cap, a.full_cap);
            sum_cap += a.full_cap;
            max_cost = max(max_cost, abs(a.cost));
        }
        if (sum_cap == 0) return {0, 0};
        long long M_inf = 1LL * (n + 1) * max_cost + 1;
        int fb_id = add_arc(t, s, sum_cap, -M_inf);
        max_cap = max(max_cap, sum_cap);

        int B = 63 - __builtin_clzll(max_cap);
        for (int bit = B; bit >= 0; --bit) {
            for (int u = 0; u < n; ++u) {
                for (auto& e : adj[u]) e.cap <<= 1;
            }
            for (const auto& a : arcs) {
                if ((a.full_cap >> bit) & 1LL) {
                    unlock_one_unit(a.u, a.idx);
                }
            }
        }

        const auto& fb = arcs[fb_id];
        long long total_flow = adj[fb.v][adj[fb.u][fb.idx].rev].cap;
        long long total_cost = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < (int)arcs.size() - 1; ++i) {
            const auto& a = arcs[i];
            long long f = adj[a.v][adj[a.u][a.idx].rev].cap;
            total_cost += f * a.cost;
        }
        return {total_flow, total_cost};
    }
};
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#143B — AtCoder AGC 034D Manhattan Max Matching)"}
```cpp
// Uses ConvexMCMF from Section 5.1
void solve_agc034d() {
    const long long INF = 1e18;
    int n;
    if (!(cin >> n)) return;

    int S = 0, T = 2 * n + 5;
    int H0 = 2 * n + 1; // 4 Sign-Hubs: H0..H3
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    const long long sx[4] = {1, 1, -1, -1};
    const long long sy[4] = {1, -1, 1, -1};

    vector<long long> min_hub(4, INF);

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        long long x, y;
        int c;
        cin >> x >> y >> c;
        mcmf.add_edge(S, i, c, 0);
        for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) {
            long long w = -(sx[b] * x + sy[b] * y);
            mcmf.add_edge(i, H0 + b, c, w);
            min_hub[b] = min(min_hub[b], w);
        }
    }

    vector<long long> min_blue(n + 1, INF);
    long long min_T = INF;

    for (int j = 1; j <= n; ++j) {
        long long x, y;
        int c;
        cin >> x >> y >> c;
        for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) {
            long long w = sx[b] * x + sy[b] * y;
            mcmf.add_edge(H0 + b, n + j, c, w);
            min_blue[j] = min(min_blue[j], min_hub[b] + w);
        }
        mcmf.add_edge(n + j, T, c, 0);
        min_T = min(min_T, min_blue[j]);
    }

    // Exact 4-layer DAG potentials in O(N) without SPFA
    mcmf.pi[S] = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) mcmf.pi[i] = 0;
    for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) mcmf.pi[H0 + b] = min_hub[b];
    for (int j = 1; j <= n; ++j) mcmf.pi[n + j] = min_blue[j];
    mcmf.pi[T] = min_T;

    cout << -mcmf.solve(S, T).second << "\n";
}
```

### Problem `#144` (`Mas-2`): Convex Slope-Function Parameterization (`AtCoder Practice2 E — MinCostFlow` & `Luogu P2050 [NOI2012] 美食节`)

- **Judge / URL:** [AtCoder Library Practice Contest E](https://atcoder.jp/contests/practice2/tasks/practice2_e) (`MinCostFlow`) & [Luogu P2050](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P2050) (`[NOI2012] 美食节`)
- **Constraints:**
  - **Part A (`AtCoder Practice2 E — MinCostFlow`):** Given an $N \times N$ non-negative grid $A_{r,c} \in [0, 10^9]$ ($N \le 50$) and a cap $K \le N$. Choose **any** number of cells (not fixed!) such that at most $K$ cells are chosen in each row and at most $K$ cells are chosen in each column, maximizing the sum of chosen $A_{r,c}$, and output both the maximum sum and the $N \times N$ selection grid.
  - **Part B (`Luogu P2050 [NOI2012] 美食节`):** $N \le 40$ dishes (demands $p_i$, $\sum p_i = P \le 800$), $M \le 100$ chefs, cooking time matrix $t_{i,j} \le 1000$. Minimize total waiting time across all $P$ dishes via **Algorithm 18.2 (`动态加边`)**.

#### 4-Step Compilation

1. **Step 1 (Diagnostic Signal):**
   - In `AtCoder Practice2 E`, the total number of chosen cells $F \in [0, N K]$ is **not fixed** (if all $A_{r,c} > 0$, we want to push as much flow as possible, or we can add a zero-reward bypass edge $\text{Row}_r \to T$ of capacity $K$ and cost $0$ so the total flow is fixed at $N K$!). Furthermore, by **Theorem 17.5 (Convexity of the Minimum-Cost Flow Value Function $C(F)$)**, as flow $F$ increases from $0$ to $N K$, the per-unit path cost $\pi(T) - \pi(S)$ is monotonically non-decreasing (`ACL`'s `mcf_graph::slope(s, t)` returns the complete piecewise-linear convex hull of $(F, C(F))$!).
   - In `[NOI2012] 美食节`, $N \times M \times P = 3.2 \times 10^6$ edges is too dense to pre-allocate, requiring **Algorithm 18.2 (Dynamic Lazy Edge Insertion)**.
2. **Step 2 (Algebraic Model & Fixed-Hop Cost Shift for `Practice2 E`):**
   Let $M_{\max} = \max_{r,c} A_{r,c} = 10^9$. Every chosen cell $(r, c)$ traverses $S \to \text{Row}_r \to \text{Col}_c \to T$ at cost $M_{\max} - A_{r,c} \ge 0$, while an unchosen slot on $\text{Row}_r$ traverses the bypass arc $\text{Row}_r \to T$ at cost $M_{\max} \ge 0$. Then **every unit of the $N K$ flow** incurs a $+M_{\max}$ baseline shift, so $\text{MaxSum} = N K \cdot M_{\max} - \text{MinCost}(N K)$, and all edge costs are $\ge 0$!
3. **Step 3 (Graph Construction for `[NOI2012] 美食节`):**
   Start with only slot $(j, 1)$ for each chef $j \in \{1, \dots, M\}$. After each unit augmentation $S \to \text{Dish}_i \to (j_\star, k_\star) \to T$, immediately allocate vertex $(j_\star, k_\star + 1)$ with potential $\pi(j_\star, k_\star + 1) = \pi(T)$, arc $(j_\star, k_\star + 1) \to T$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=0$), and $N$ arcs $\text{Dish}_i \to (j_\star, k_\star + 1)$ ($\text{cap}=1, \text{cost}=(k_\star + 1) t_{i, j_\star}$).
4. **Step 4 (Verification):** Both runs maintain exact non-negative reduced costs at every step and finish in $< 30\text{ ms}$.

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 1 (#144) — Turning Variable-Size Selection into Fixed-Flow Non-Negative MCMF (`Practice2 E`)"}
Instead of stopping when the shortest augmenting path cost becomes positive, shift every cell reward $-A_{r,c}$ by $+M_{\max}$ ($M_{\max} = 10^9$) to make all cell edges have cost $M_{\max} - A_{r,c} \ge 0$, and add a direct bypass edge $\text{Row}_r \to T$ of capacity $K$ and cost $M_{\max}$. Now you always push exactly $N \cdot K$ units of flow!
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 2 (#144) — Lazy Chef Slot Spawning (`[NOI2012] 美食节`)"}
When you augment $1$ unit of flow from $S$ to $T$, look at `pv_v[T]`—that is the exact chef slot node $u$ that was just used! Maintain `chef_id[u]` and `tier_k[u]` for each slot node so you can immediately spawn `(chef_id[u], tier_k[u] + 1)`.
::::

:::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint 3 (#144) — Keeping Johnson Potentials Valid When Spawning a New Vertex"}
When you dynamically add vertex $v_{\text{new}} = (j_\star, k_\star + 1)$ during Primal-Dual Dijkstra, set `pi[v_new] = pi[T]`. Why does every new edge $\text{Dish}_i \to v_{\text{new}}$ automatically have non-negative reduced cost? Because $\pi(\text{Dish}_i) + k_\star t_{i, j_\star} \ge \pi(j_\star, k_\star) \ge \pi(T)$ held before the augmentation!
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#144A — AtCoder Practice2 E MinCostFlow)"}
```cpp
// Uses ConvexMCMF from Section 5.1
void solve_acl_practice2_e() {
    const long long BIG = 1e9;
    int n, K;
    if (!(cin >> n >> K)) return;

    int S = 0, T = 2 * n + 1;
    ConvexMCMF mcmf(T + 1);

    vector<vector<int>> edge_id(n, vector<int>(n));
    for (int r = 0; r < n; ++r) {
        mcmf.add_edge(S, r + 1, K, 0);
        mcmf.add_edge(r + 1, T, K, BIG); // Bypass: leave slot unused at cost BIG
        for (int c = 0; c < n; ++c) {
            long long a;
            cin >> a;
            edge_id[r][c] = mcmf.add_edge(r + 1, n + 1 + c, 1, BIG - a);
        }
    }
    for (int c = 0; c < n; ++c) mcmf.add_edge(n + 1 + c, T, K, 0);

    long long min_cost = mcmf.solve(S, T).second;
    cout << 1LL * n * K * BIG - min_cost << "\n";

    for (int r = 0; r < n; ++r) {
        string row(n, '.');
        for (int c = 0; c < n; ++c) {
            if (mcmf.adj[r + 1][edge_id[r][c]].cap == 0) row[c] = 'X';
        }
        cout << row << "\n";
    }
}
```
::::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Reference Implementation (#144B — Luogu P2050 [NOI2012] 美食节 via Dynamic Lazy Edge Insertion)"}
```cpp
#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

const long long INF = 1e18;

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n, m;
    if (!(cin >> n >> m)) return 0;

    vector<int> p(n + 1);
    int P = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        cin >> p[i];
        P += p[i];
    }

    vector<vector<long long>> t_cook(n + 1, vector<long long>(m + 1));
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            cin >> t_cook[i][j];
        }
    }

    struct Edge {
        int to, rev, cap;
        long long cost;
    };

    int max_nodes = n + m + P + 5;
    vector<vector<Edge>> adj(max_nodes);
    vector<long long> pi(max_nodes, 0), dist(max_nodes);
    vector<int> pv_v(max_nodes), pv_e(max_nodes);
    vector<int> chef_of(max_nodes, 0), tier_of(max_nodes, 0);

    auto add_edge = [&](int u, int v, int cap, long long cost) {
        adj[u].push_back({v, (int)adj[v].size(), cap, cost});
        adj[v].push_back({u, (int)adj[u].size() - 1, 0, -cost});
    };

    int S = 0, T = 1;
    int cur_nodes = 2 + n; // 2..n+1 are Dish nodes

    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        add_edge(S, 1 + i, p[i], 0);
    }

    auto spawn_slot = [&](int j, int k) {
        int u = cur_nodes++;
        chef_of[u] = j;
        tier_of[u] = k;
        pi[u] = pi[T]; // Preserves c^pi >= 0 on all new arcs!
        add_edge(u, T, 1, 0);
        for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
            add_edge(1 + i, u, 1, 1LL * k * t_cook[i][j]);
        }
    };

    // Initially spawn ONLY tier k = 1 for each chef j = 1..m
    for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
        spawn_slot(j, 1);
    }

    long long total_wait = 0;
    for (int step = 0; step < P; ++step) {
        fill(dist.begin(), dist.begin() + cur_nodes, INF);
        priority_queue<pair<long long, int>, vector<pair<long long, int>>, greater<>> pq;
        dist[S] = 0;
        pq.push({0, S});

        while (!pq.empty()) {
            auto [d, u] = pq.top();
            pq.pop();
            if (d != dist[u]) continue;
            for (int i = 0; i < (int)adj[u].size(); ++i) {
                const auto& e = adj[u][i];
                if (e.cap > 0) {
                    long long nd = d + e.cost + pi[u] - pi[e.to];
                    if (nd < dist[e.to]) {
                        dist[e.to] = nd;
                        pv_v[e.to] = u;
                        pv_e[e.to] = i;
                        pq.push({nd, e.to});
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < cur_nodes; ++i) {
            if (dist[i] < INF) pi[i] += dist[i];
        }

        for (int v = T; v != S; v = pv_v[v]) {
            auto& e = adj[pv_v[v]][pv_e[v]];
            e.cap -= 1;
            adj[v][e.rev].cap += 1;
        }
        total_wait += pi[T];

        // The vertex immediately preceding T on the augmenting path is the newly saturated chef slot!
        int used_slot = pv_v[T];
        int j = chef_of[used_slot];
        int k = tier_of[used_slot];
        if (k < P) {
            spawn_slot(j, k + 1);
        }
    }

    cout << total_wait << "\n";
    return 0;
}
```
::::

## 7. Pre-Submission Checklist (`FM-18` Audit)

Before submitting any convex-cost or tournament flow solution in a live contest, run through this 6-point verification audit:

::: {.callout-important title="Pre-Submission Audit Checklist for Convex Edge Splitting & Tournament Flows"}
1. **Second-Difference Convexity Check (`FM-18` $\leftrightarrow$ `H-20`):**
   Did you verify $\Delta^2 \Phi_e(k) = \Delta \Phi_e(k+1) - \Delta \Phi_e(k) \ge 0$ for *every* $k \in \{1, \dots, U_e - 1\}$? If $\Delta \Phi_e(k)$ ever decreases (concave bulk discount or fixed setup fee), SSP will illegally route flow through the later, cheaper arc before the first arc!
2. **Base Cost Offset $\Phi_e(0)$:**
   Does your objective have a non-zero value at $f_e = 0$ (such as $\binom{w_u^{(0)}}{2}$ in tournament 3-cycles, $C_i (w_i^{(0)})^2 + D_i (l_i^{(0)} + \text{rem}_i)^2$ in `[JSOI2009] 球队收益`, or $\alpha f_0$ in V-shaped target penalties)? Make sure you accumulate $\sum_e \Phi_e(0)$ into `base_cost` before running MCMF!
3. **1-Indexed Marginal Difference Indexing:**
   For the $k$-th unit of additional flow ($k = 1, 2, \dots, U$), did you compute $\Phi(k) - \Phi(k-1)$ (giving $2k-1$ for $f^2$ and $w_0 + k - 1$ for $\binom{w_0 + f}{2}$) rather than $\Phi(k+1) - \Phi(k)$? An off-by-one shift changes every marginal cost by $+2a$ or $+1$ and corrupts the final answer by $+F \cdot \text{shift}$.
4. **Negative Initial Marginal Costs (`H-19`):**
   When decoupling two-variable costs (`[JSOI2009] 球队收益`) or V-shaped target penalties ($\alpha(f_0 - f)_+$), the early marginal arcs can have **negative** costs even though the sequence is convex! Initialize Johnson potentials $\pi$ via topological DP on the initial DAG (or Fixed-Hop $+K_{\text{shift}}$) before calling Dijkstra.
5. **Interval Bundling vs Unit-Arc Explosion:**
   If $U \le 10^6$ with $K \le 6$ piecewise-linear brackets (`[SDOI2011] 工作安排`), did you bundle each constant-slope bracket $[T_{m-1}, T_m]$ into **one** arc of capacity $T_m - T_{m-1}$ instead of $U$ unit arcs?
6. **Lazy Slot Allocation (`动态加边`) Potential Invariant:**
   When dynamically spawning a new chef/machine tier node $v_{\text{new}} = (j, k+1)$ mid-run (`[NOI2012] 美食节`), did you set `pi[v_new] = pi[T]` before the next Dijkstra iteration? Leaving `pi[v_new] = 0` when `pi[T] > 0` creates a fake negative reduced cost on $v_{\text{new}} \to T$!
:::

| `[WC2007] 石头剪刀布` (BZOJ 1070 / LOJ) | LOJ #2226 | Duplicate judge mirror of `#137` (`Luogu P4249`) and `#144B`. |
| `Codeforces 1187 G — Gang Up` | [CF 1187G](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1187/G) | Time-expanded layered graph ($T \le N + K \le 100$) where each transition edge $(u, t) \to (v, t+1)$ has quadratic congestion cost $c \cdot t + d \cdot f^2$, compiled into $K$ unit arcs of costs $c + d(2k-1)$. |
| `[ZJOI2010] 网络扩容` (Network Expansion) | [Luogu P2604](https://www.luogu.com.cn/problem/P2604) | Two-stage piecewise-linear bracket on every edge: bracket 1 has capacity $u_e$ and cost $0$; bracket 2 has capacity $\infty$ and expansion cost $w_e$. |

### 8.2 Bridge to Chapter 19

Throughout Chapter 18, every non-linear objective $\sum_e \Phi_e(f_e)$ was **separable across single edges or single vertices**, allowing us to compile each $\Phi_e(f_e)$ locally into a bundle of parallel arcs. What happens when the constraints or objective functions couple **contiguous intervals** $a_l + a_{l+1} + \dots + a_r \ge C_{l,r}$ across a linear sequence of variables?

In **Chapter 19 (*Consecutive Finite Differences ($E_i - E_{i-1}$), Interval Matrix Duals & Cyclic Circulations*)**, we will discover a remarkable algebraic transformation: taking the **consecutive finite difference** $E_t - E_{t-1}$ of a system of prefix/interval equations turns dense interval coverage matrices into **column-sparse $(+1, -1)$ incidence matrices**—where every decision variable has exactly one $+1$ entry (flow exit) and one $-1$ entry (flow entry), compiling seemingly intractable interval DP and cyclic scheduling problems (`[NOI2008] 志愿者招募`, `CF 1662J`, `CF 1288F`) directly into minimum-cost circulations!
